title: Evaluation of a degree-one polynomial
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $p$ be a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of $[n]$, and suppose $p(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>1$. Then for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, \[\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}p(S)\chi_S(x)=p(\varnothing)+\sum_{i\in[n]}p(\{i\})(-1)^{x_i}.\]
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of $[n]$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients $a_S$. If $a_S=0$ for $|S|>1$, then $P(x)=a_\varnothing+\sum_{i=1}^n a_{\{i\}}(-1)^{x_i}$ for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$.
